summary.name: Zimbra
summary.one_liner: Zimbra is an email, calendar, file storage, chat and collaboration platform built on open standards, deployable on-premises, in private cloud, or via regional data centers.
use_cases: Hosting company email and calendars on-premises
Meeting data residency and compliance rules
Syncing email to mobile devices via ActiveSync
Sharing team files and chat in one server
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Zimbra as a collaboration suite covering email, shared calendars, Briefcase server-side file storage with permissions and version tracking, and basic and advanced chat with file sharing and channels. It offers in-browser editing for documents, spreadsheets and slides, with support for many office formats. Clients listed include web, Exchange ActiveSync for mobile, Zimbra Connector for Outlook, Exchange Web Services, and an offline desktop client. Security features named include 2FA, S/MIME, SAML SSO (with Keycloak, Cisco Duo, JumpCloud), compliance archiving, mobile device management, multi-tenancy, delegated administration, and backup and restore. The page also cites a source code listing of GPL-2.0/CPAL-1.0 licensed Java code, and emphasises auditable open code.
notable: Open, auditable code licensed GPL-2.0/CPAL-1.0 with Java source
Hierarchical storage management to offload old email to S3-compatible object stores
Deployment on-premises, private cloud or regional data centers for data residency
Multi-tenancy and delegated administration on a single instance
caveats: Pricing is tiered into Standard and Professional plans with Premier or Standard support levels, and some features (e.g. Outlook for Windows, mobile push, archiving) appear only in certain plans
Page emphasises enterprise sales and partner-led deployment rather than free use
